topic: How does L-DACS integration impact spectrum sharing between A2G and satellite links in congested airspaces?
consensus_response: L-DACS integration into congested airspaces exacerbates interference between A2G and satellite links due to shared frequency bands, compromising spectrum sharing. The presence of Non-Linear Amplifiers (NLAs) introduces non-linear distortions affecting signal quality and interference mitigation. Robust A2A communication protocols like RLC PDCP can mitigate this interference by adapting to changing channel conditions. However, in parallel satellite and terrestrial link scenarios, traffic needs to be distributed onto both links based on its requirements and the links' capabilities. This requires additional complexity in terms of capacity loss, as the system must allocate resources for optimal traffic distribution.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of channel-induced dispersion in A2A communication scenarios, with rapidly fluctuating frequency-selective fading due to the high velocity of aircraft. The ICAO has recommended further development and evaluation of L-DACS technology candidates, including L-DACS1 and L-DACS2. The literature emphasizes the need for tight coordination between satellite and terrestrial networks when sharing frequencies.
